messages:
Devon (Customer): Hi, weve had our app start losing SSE output intermittently after putting Cloudflare in front of our ALB. The client (EventSource in browser) receives a few events, then nothing for ~28s and then connection closes without any final event. The client reconnects (EventSource auto) but the resumed stream only sometimes contains the missing data. This began right after enabling Cloudflare proxying for api.mycorp.example.

Priya (Support): Thanks Devon. Well help debug. Can you share a small repro (curl) and any origin / ALB logs you have? Also which CF plan and any Page Rules/Workers?

Devon (Customer): Repro were using from terminal:

```
# force HTTP/1.1 to compare
curl -v -N --http1.1 \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACT>" \
  https://api.mycorp.example/v1/stream/live
```

Observed: stream starts, we get a few `data:` events and `: hb` heartbeats, then stop getting bytes. curl stays open for ~28s then prints `Connection reset by peer` and exits. Origin logs show repeated `write: broken pipe` and our ALB access logs include lines with `target_status_code: -1` and `elb_status_code: 200` for the same request.

Priya (Support): Helpful. Are you terminating TLS at Cloudflare and proxying to the ALB? Any HTTP/2-to-origin enabled on Cloudflare? Do you have Argo or any Workers that could buffer responses?

Devon (Customer): Yes TLS at CF edge, proxying to ALB. No Workers. HTTP/2 on the client <-> CF side is enabled by default. We havent changed ALB idle timeout (default 60s). No special page rules.

Eli (Edge): Flagging eng-edge. This smells like a middlebox idle/flow-control mismatch between CF -> ALB -> origin. Two common paths cause truncated SSE: 1) Cloudflare (or another proxy) converts client h2 -> origin h1/1 and buffers until a window is filled, then when the origin writes slowly the proxied TCP may be closed while the edge keeps the client side open. 2) HTTP/2 flow control window exhaustion or RST_STREAM propagation when the downstream path expects different keepalive behavior. The ALB reporting target_status_code -1 is consistent with the target (origin) dropping the TCP while the client-side proxy finished with 200.

Jules (Runtime): Quick checklist weve used internally to isolate:
- Confirm Transfer-Encoding: chunked and that your app flushes after every SSE event. In Go use `w.(http.Flusher).Flush()`, in Node `res.flush()` / `res.write` + `res.flushHeaders()`.
- Add an SSE comment heartbeat every 10-15s: `: heartbeat\n\n` to keep CF/ALB from idling the connection.
- For nginx origins, return header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and set `proxy_buffering off;` for the upstream location. For envoy, ensure `use_remote_address` / `stream_idle_timeout` are tuned and that HTTP/2 flow control params are default.
- Test bypassing Cloudflare (DNS or host header to origin) to see if problem follows the origin or only when CF is in path.

Priya (Support): Also try forcing HTTP/1.1 on the client/CURL (you already did), and if possible force CF to use HTTP/1.1 to the origin for a test (some CF plans let you toggle origin protocol settings) because HTTP/2 -> origin can change behavior.

Devon (Customer): We tested direct origin (bypassed CF) and the stream stayed healthy for >10 minutes. When going through CF it fails in ~28s. Forcing `--http1.1` to the CF endpoint didn't change behavior (CF still speaks to origin in its chosen protocol).

Eli (Edge): Given that bypassing CF fixes it, this is almost certainly Cloudflare buffering/idle behaviour. Workarounds:
- Ensure your origin sends frequent small writes (heartbeats) and flushes immediately.
- Add `Cache-Control: no-transform, no-cache` and `Connection: keep-alive` on SSE responses (CF respects no-transform in some cases).
- Try setting `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) or the equivalent in your app framework.
- If you can, increase ALB idle timeout above 60s (to 300s) so the whole path has a larger headroom while you test.

Jules (Runtime): Config snippets we use:

nginx upstream location example:
```
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
}
```

Node/Express SSE example:
```
res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-cache, no-transform');
res.setHeader('Connection', 'keep-alive');
res.write(': heartbeat\\n\\n'); // send initial
setInterval(() => { res.write(': heartbeat\\n\\n'); res.flush && res.flush(); }, 15000);
```

Jules (Runtime): Also watch for library-level buffering (some frameworks will buffer until a threshold). If youre behind ALB + nginx, the combination can hide the problem until CF+ALB interaction triggers a mid-stream close.

Priya (Support): Action items for us to help: can you share an ALB access log entry (anonymized) and the raw TCP-level client curl output for a failing request? We can escalate to CF support with those traces.

Devon (Customer): Attached two log snippets below (anonymized):

ALB line: `https 2023-11-02T14:23:12.345Z app/myalb/abcd 10.0.0.1:443 10.0.0.2:56789 0.000 28.123 0.000 200 -1 1234 5678 "GET https://api.mycorp.example/v1/stream/live HTTP/1.1"`

Server stderr: `2023-11-02T14:23:40Z write tcp 10.0.0.2:56789->10.0.0.1:443: write: broken pipe`

curl output: `* Connection #0 to host api.mycorp.example left intact
* Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`

Priya (Support): Thanks. Next steps: 1) Well open an internal ticket with CF with these logs and ask them to check if edge is buffering or issuing RST to origin. 2) Please try adding an aggressive heartbeat (every 10s) and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on origin; report back. 3) If convenient, temporarily point a hostname straight to your ALB (bypass CF) and confirm tests (you already tried successfully).

deploy-bot: rollout/edge-keepalive-patches v2 started (canary -> 10%). This patch adds more conservative HTTP/2 flow-control handling at our side; monitor for reduced truncations.

Eli (Edge): One final note: some clients (mobile networks) will aggressively NAT timeout connections ~30s. Heartbeats solve both proxy and mobile NAT issues. If you still see failures after the above, well correlate timing and escalate to CF with packet traces.

Devon (Customer): Will implement heartbeat + X-Accel and report back within the day. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
